newsitem.title: USA: Negotiations to end Coca-Cola suit continue.
newsitem.headline: Negotiations to end Coca-Cola suit continue.

text.p: Negotiations between Babson Bros Co and Coca-Cola Co to settle a trademark dilution lawsuit filed against the soda giant continued Wednesday, the eve of the next court hearing on the issue.
"Talks are taking place today," said a spokeswoman for Babson Bros, which makes dairy and agricultural products.

At the heart of the dispute is Coke's plan to launch a new high-caffeine soft drink this weekend under the brand name Surge. Babson contends it has held a trademark on the name since 1925 for its automatic milking machine and industrial cleaning products.
The two sides have been in discussions since Tuesday and they are scheduled to meet before a U.S. District Court in Chicago tomorrow, spokeswomen for both companies said.
The suit, originally filed December 23, seeks to stop Coke from using the Surge name until all legal issues are settled.

In a prepared statement, Babson officials said their case is based on trademark dilution regarding the Surge brand name and trademark infringement with regard to clothing and promotional items Coke allegedly plans to market using Surge.
Babson also believes there may be a health risk if consumers confuse its green-colored cleaning products with the green soft drink Coke plans to use to challenge PepsiCo Inc's Mountain Dew beverage.
Babson is based in Naperville, Illinois.
Preventing public confusion is among the issues currently being discussed, Babson officials said in a press release.
The suit was filed as Coke prepared an advertising campaign for Surge at this Sunday's Super Bowl contest.
"At this point, we plan to advertise Surge on the Super Bowl in some markets and Diet Coke in other parts of the country," said a Coca-Cola spokeswoman, who declined to comment on the lawsuit.
